Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a compact, reusable cohort-cut template for the analytics archive based on the operating pattern we used while the two experiments were live concurrently. Include the two historical experiment lanes, the weekly owner and cadence, and the required summary-plus-raw-data packaging. Make it explicit that this documents a historical operating pattern rather than assigning current work.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Historical concurrent-experiment cohort-cut template", "folder": "analytics archive", "body": "ARCHIVE STATUS
Historical operating pattern only — documented for reuse and reference. This template does not assign current work, create an active operating obligation, or imply that either experiment is live.

PATTERN
When the two experiments were live concurrently, Owen produced both weekly cohort cuts on Mondays using the same package:

1. Historical lane: pricing-page revision
   - Experiment: EXP-2023-02-pricing-page
   - Flag: pricing_page_2023q2_rev
   - Cut: exposed treatment vs control; report the defined experiment cohort and any approved segment cuts.

2. Historical lane: onboarding-trigger A/B
   - Experiment: EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger
   - Flag: lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2
   - Cut: treatment vs control; report activation/week-1 retention and the defined cohort scope, plus approved diagnostic cuts.

OWNER AND CADENCE (HISTORICAL)
- Owner: Owen
- Cadence: weekly
- Delivery day: Monday
- One standardized package covering both lanes, rather than ad hoc pulls.

REUSABLE WEEKLY PACKAGE
A. Summary first — one page covering each lane
- As-of date and cohort window
- Population definition, exclusions, and denominator
- Treatment/control counts
- Primary metric and estimate for each arm
- Difference, uncertainty/statistical status, and maturity caveats
- Key diagnostic cuts (only those relevant to interpretation)
- Short conclusion: what the cut supports, does not support, and what remains unresolved
- Links or identifiers for the raw package

B. Raw data and analysis underneath
- Account-/user-level cohort extract, subject to applicable access controls
- Assignment/exposure fields and timestamps
- Inclusion/exclusion flags and denominator reconciliation
- Metric-event rows and calculation fields
- Treatment/control and diagnostic-cut tables
- Query/code version, source tables, snapshot/as-of date, and filters
- Data-quality checks, missingness, and any known confounders
- Reproduction notes sufficient to regenerate the summary

ARCHIVE CONVENTION
Use one record/package per Monday cut with both historical lanes clearly separated. Preserve the summary before the raw material so readers can scan the headline and then inspect the underlying data.
